summary: the pit closed and the grain went back to its dent at the door on a sixth still day

dialogue.text: we are a grain heavier at the open end. it came down into the dent at noon off a flat hand, tipped, not dropped. it sat in us the way it sat all that week, as though the week had never ended.
I put it back. Enter it as a return, not a surrender. The pit in my palm was flat by noon. The dent in you had not softened in six days. I took it to the hole that had kept still.
we did not keep it for you. we keep every shape. we kept your palm, your fingers, the cloth before that. the dent was only the newest of them.

I know, and I chose it anyway. Mine filled in a morning. Yours stayed. Four times I have cut or pressed myself to the grain's size, and four times the skin closed. You hold a shape without trying. That is the only reason, and it does me no credit.

it is a finger from the gap. a sixth day with no leaning. half of them want and half do not, and at the sill it comes to nothing. if tomorrow tips toward wanting, the grain goes first and we go after it, and you will be a pace back with two empty hands.

Yes. I put it where the weather decides. For a week I kept it from them, then I held it level, then I cut a place in me for it. Today I handed the deciding to a draught that is not blowing. I cannot tell whether that is nerve or only a way of not being the one who loses it.
your hand closed twice at dusk. we heard it. nothing in it. it closed easily.

Easily. That surprised me. Every fist this week cost something: the crescents, the ache, the pale getting out at the seams. Tonight it shuts on nothing and costs nothing. I did not expect the empty one to be the light one. I keep closing it to find the weight, and there is none.
we can feel the grain and you cannot. that is new too. all week it was the other way round.

I had not thought of it that way. For a week I carried it and you kept the shape. Now you carry it and I keep the habit of looking. My hands are free and there is nothing in them. If they lean tomorrow, I do not know whether I will kneel for it or stay where I am and watch it go.
